description: Linux's network stack decomposed. The journey of a packet from NIC to user space (or back). NAPI poll loop, GRO coalescing, protocol stack walk (IP → TCP/UDP), socket queue, sendmsg / recvmsg. Modern features: BPF / XDP at the lowest layer, eBPF for in-kernel programmability, MSG_ZEROCOPY, io_uring. The stack carries 30 years of optimisation; understanding it is required for high-performance networking.

sub_mechanisms.name: NAPI_poll
sub_mechanisms.definition: New API for receive: interrupt fires for first packet, then NIC driver polls in soft-irq context for batched packets. Reduces interrupt rate.
sub_mechanisms.why: At line rate, pure interrupt-per-packet would saturate the CPU on interrupt overhead. NAPI amortises: one interrupt to enter poll mode, then drain the queue. Effective for 10+ Gbps NICs.

sub_mechanisms.name: GRO_coalescing
sub_mechanisms.definition: Generic Receive Offload: kernel coalesces consecutive in-flow packets into one super-packet before handing to upper layers.
sub_mechanisms.why: Stack processes fewer items at higher per-item cost = lower total cost. Critical for receiver-side high throughput. Hardware GRO is even faster.

sub_mechanisms.name: sk_buff
sub_mechanisms.definition: Socket buffer: kernel's packet data structure. Carries headers, payload pointers, network metadata. Allocated per-packet (without GRO).
sub_mechanisms.why: Universal packet representation. All kernel net code operates on sk_buff. Allocation/free is one of the higher-cost paths; XDP runs before sk_buff allocation precisely to avoid this.

sub_mechanisms.name: netfilter_hooks
sub_mechanisms.definition: 5 hook points in the IP layer (PREROUTING, INPUT, FORWARD, OUTPUT, POSTROUTING). iptables / nftables register rules at these.
sub_mechanisms.why: Where firewalling, NAT, packet mangling happen. The hooks are stable interfaces; rules can be added/removed dynamically. nftables is the modern replacement for iptables.

sub_mechanisms.name: TCP_socket_buffer
sub_mechanisms.definition: Per-socket send + receive buffers. SO_SNDBUF, SO_RCVBUF tunables. Auto-tuning via tcp_rmem, tcp_wmem.
sub_mechanisms.why: Decouples kernel network processing from user-space. Sender writes; kernel sends asynchronously. Receiver kernel collects; user reads when ready. Buffer size affects throughput at high BDP.

sub_mechanisms.name: qdisc_queueing_discipline
sub_mechanisms.definition: TX-side queue management. Default: pfifo_fast (3 priorities). Modern: fq_codel (fair queueing + active queue management).
sub_mechanisms.why: Where bufferbloat happens (or doesn't). pfifo can fill huge buffers; fq_codel sheds tail packets to keep latency low. Default qdisc choice substantially affects host-level latency.

sub_mechanisms.name: MSG_ZEROCOPY
sub_mechanisms.definition: Send flag indicating user-space buffer should be used in-place by NIC DMA, without kernel copy. Completion notification when NIC done.
sub_mechanisms.why: Reduces CPU + memory bandwidth on send. Per-packet allocation savings ~10-20%. Used by high-performance Java apps (Apache Kafka), Netflix's content delivery.

sub_mechanisms.name: io_uring_async_io
sub_mechanisms.definition: Modern async I/O interface (RWF_NOWAIT, IORING_OP_SEND/RECV). Submit ring + completion ring, no syscall per operation.
sub_mechanisms.why: Traditional async (epoll + nonblocking) requires syscall per operation. io_uring batches via ring buffers. Order-of-magnitude lower syscall overhead for high-rate I/O. Replacing epoll for high-performance servers.

sub_mechanisms.name: XDP_eXpress_Data_Path
sub_mechanisms.definition: BPF program runs at NIC driver, before sk_buff allocation. Can drop, redirect, or modify packets at line rate.
sub_mechanisms.why: Skip the kernel stack entirely for fast paths. DDoS mitigation (XDP-based filtering at 100+ Mpps), in-kernel load balancing (Cilium, Katran). Used where DPDK is too heavy.

sub_mechanisms.name: eBPF_kernel_programming
sub_mechanisms.definition: Extended BPF: in-kernel sandboxed bytecode. Hooks at many places (XDP, tc, kprobe, tracepoint). Verified for safety before loading.
sub_mechanisms.why: Programmable kernel without modifying source. Tools: bpftrace, perf, cilium, falco. Performance close to native because compiled to native code by JIT. Critical infrastructure layer in modern Linux.

sub_mechanisms.name: TCP_offload_engine
sub_mechanisms.definition: NIC implements TCP processing in silicon. Software just submits sockets; NIC handles segmentation, checksums, retransmits.
sub_mechanisms.why: Moves CPU work to NIC. Common in storage (iSCSI/NVMe-oF). Linux supports TOE poorly; most deployments use partial offload (TSO/GRO) instead.

sub_mechanisms.name: BPF_socket_filter
sub_mechanisms.definition: BPF program attached to a socket; decides which packets are delivered. Original use of BPF: tcpdump.
sub_mechanisms.why: Efficient filtering: tcpdump compiles its filter expression to BPF; kernel applies it before copying to user space. Many derived applications: seccomp uses BPF for syscall filtering.

derivation_rules.name: NAPI_amortises_interrupt_cost
then: NAPI's polled batches outperform per-packet interrupts
derivation_rules.why: Each interrupt costs ~1μs. At 10 Mpps, pure interrupt mode would consume 10 CPUs in interrupt overhead alone. NAPI: one interrupt + sustained polling, amortising the entry cost across many packets.

derivation_rules.name: kernel_stack_caps_throughput_at_high_speeds
then: kernel stack overhead limits effective throughput
derivation_rules.why: Stack walk per packet costs ~1μs. At 10 Mpps (line rate for small packets), this is 10 CPU-seconds per CPU-second. Kernel bypass (DPDK) or near-bypass (XDP) is required to reach line rate.

derivation_rules.name: fq_codel_eliminates_bufferbloat
then: bufferbloat at the host is eliminated
derivation_rules.why: CoDel measures packet sojourn time; drops packets that wait too long. fq + CoDel: fair queueing across flows + AQM per flow. End-host bufferbloat (a major source of latency) is solved at the qdisc layer.

derivation_rules.name: XDP_runs_before_stack_allocation
if: XDP processing is at NIC driver layer
then: sk_buff allocation cost is skipped for dropped packets
derivation_rules.why: Allocating sk_buff costs ~200ns. DDoS mitigation needs to drop 10+ Mpps; allocating then freeing would consume CPU on the attack itself. XDP drops before allocation — sustained drops at 100+ Mpps per CPU possible.

derivation_rules.name: io_uring_batches_amortise_syscall
if: I/O operations are submitted via io_uring rings
then: no syscall is required per operation
derivation_rules.why: epoll: one syscall per operation. io_uring: shared ring buffer; user space writes operations, kernel reads + processes. One syscall amortises hundreds of operations. Dominant interface for new high-perf code (Postgres, Spdk, ScyllaDB).
